request.note: Any payload (an object, a string, a number). The server does not read it: it sends it with no change to the socket of the followed character. Observer sockets only.

confirm.note: The wrapper turns an `undefined` payload into `{}`

responses.name: Success
responses.when: All checks pass. The payload goes to the followed character as `code_eval` (see below); the observer gets nothing.

rows.when: The socket is not an observer (no `observers[socket.id]`).

The observer follows no character, or the character disconnected (`player.dc`). A broadcast observer (`broadcast=1` query) follows no character, so it always ends here (node/test/observer_broadcast.test.js:102).

also.to: the socket of the followed character
also.when: All checks pass. The payload is your payload, with no change (`{}` when you sent none).

order: `code_eval` with your payload to the character (nothing to you)
